description: Statements of the published sources SCI-03 and SCI-19 that the instruments cite, each with the verbatim excerpts that carry it. A statement says what the source says, not that it is true of the valley today. Excerpts are checked against the stored page text (private corpus, not redistributed) by `verifyEvidenceExcerpts`; the stored text is not in this repository.

statements.statement: SCI-19 places the Aït Bouguemez valley between 1800 and 2200 m altitude, in the rural district of Tabant, Province of Azilal.
statements.uncertainty: As published (Auclair et al. 2011); a rounded range quoted from the source, not a measurement by Siterra.

locators.excerpt: between 1800 and 2200 m altitude in the rural district of Tabant, Province of Azilal

statements.statement: SCI-19 says the valley shelters more than thirty villages along its bottom, with a population of approximately 15,000 inhabitants.
statements.uncertainty: As published (Auclair et al. 2011); a count and a population quoted from the source, not a measurement by Siterra.

locators.excerpt: It shelters more than thirty villages stretching along the bottom of the valley, with a population of approximately 15,000 inhabitants

statements.statement: SCI-03 describes the cultivated land at the valley bottom as lying at 1800 to 2200 m and used mainly for subsistence crops and apple orchards.
statements.uncertainty: As published (El Aayadi et al. 2026); the range describes the livestock system the paper studies, quoted from the source.

locators.excerpt: the cultivated land at the valley bottom (1800–2200 m), mainly used for subsistence crops (cereals, vegetables such as potatoes and salsify, etc.) and apple orchards

statements.statement: SCI-19 describes the upper parts of the valley as extensive rangelands, mainly spiny xerophytic vegetation with reduced areas of short grasslands.
statements.uncertainty: As published (Auclair et al. 2011); a description of vegetation types, not a survey by Siterra and not a species list.

locators.excerpt: The upper parts resemble extensive rangelands, mainly composed of spiny xerophytic vegetation and reduced areas of short grasslands

statements.statement: SCI-03 says that herders, in a study in Azilal Province, reported the disappearance of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis).
statements.uncertainty: Reported perception of herders in a study the paper cites (its reference 10), in Azilal Province; not measured by Siterra and not specific to one valley. No species spectrum exists in the case.

locators.excerpt: A study in Azilal Province highlights a clear decline in the availability and quality of pastoral resources as perceived by herders [10]
Herders reported observable changes in rangeland conditions, with variations linked to altitude.
the disappearance of palatable species (e.g., Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides), and the spread of
unpalatable plants (e.g., Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) [10]
